name: Muhammad Iqbal
role: Poet-philosopher and Muslim League president (1930), Punjab Legislative Council member (1927–1930)
summary: Poet and philosopher of colonial India who argued that Islam is a unity of religion and polity, wanted its law reinterpreted by elected Muslim assemblies rather than the ulema, and criticised both Western nationalism and atheistic socialism. Politically he demanded cultural autonomy, separate electorates and a consolidated Muslim state in north-west India within a federation, and self-government from British rule.
